meta.source: 'Numerical investigation of transitional flow over Eppler 387 with k-kL-omega and transition-SST turbulence models in ANSYS Fluent', IJSRP 9(1), Jan 2019, doi 10.29322/IJSRP.9.01.2019.p8528. File: sa-ai/references/ijsrp2019-fluent-kklw-transSST-e387-polars-Re20k-300k.pdf
meta.model_coverage_note: Only the Re=60,000 section compares BOTH models (series 'Cl/Cd (k-kl)' and 'Trans SST'). The Re=100,000 and Re=300,000 sections are titled 'Analysis ... using trans-SST (model)' and their figures contain a single CFD series labeled 'numerical' (trans-SST) vs 'EXP'. No k-kL-omega results exist at Re=100k/300k in the paper; kklw is null there.
meta.experiment_note: The 'Expt.'/'EXP' series cites ref [4] = McGhee et al., NASA TM-4062 (Langley LTPT). It is digitized here as-plotted ('experiment_as_plotted') because it does NOT faithfully duplicate TM-4062: at Re=60k the plotted experimental Cl is drastically low (e.g. Cl(5 deg) ~= 0.10 vs TM-4062 ~0.63) and mirrors the (implausible) trans-SST dip; at Re=100k/300k Cl is close to TM-4062 but Cd is high (e.g. Cd ~0.019 at alpha=0, Re=100k vs TM-4062 ~0.011). Use the true TM-4062 tables for experimental comparisons, not this series.
meta.method: Although the figures RENDER as low-quality raster Excel charts, each data marker is placed in the PDF as a separate 13x13-px image XObject (xref 236=blue, 234=red, 232=green; 238=black marker shadow) with an exact vector bbox. Marker centers were taken from these bboxes and axes calibrated by least-squares on the born-digital tick-label text positions (max residual 0.00 pt; extracted alphas land on the exact integer test angles). Extraction is therefore vector-precision despite the raster look.
meta.uncertainty: Digitization uncertainty is dominated by marker-image centering, <~0.5 pt: about +/-0.02 Cl and +/-0.0006 Cd at Re=60k (small chart), +/-0.01 Cl and +/-0.0002 Cd at Re=100k/300k; alpha exact (integer grid). The dominant real uncertainty is the paper's own data quality (negative Cd at alpha=1 in Fig. 12, the Cl dip to -0.74 at 2 deg in Fig. 11 are as-plotted).
